title: Whether intellect or will contributes more to freedom is left undecided, as Aristotle left it
source_text: XLVII. An autem ad libertatem hominis plus conferat intellectus quam voluntas, aut voluntas plusquam intellectus, res est quam definire Theologi non interest, & cujus accuratiorem inquisitionem neglexit ipse hodiernorum Philosophorum Princeps Aristoteles, ac propterea nos illam cum doctissimis quibusdam Theologis in medio quoque relinquimus.
pass_a_gloss: But whether the intellect contributes more to the liberty of man than the will, or the will more than the intellect, is a thing which it does not concern the Theologian to define, & the more accurate inquiry of which Aristotle himself the Prince of the Philosophers of today neglected, and therefore we also with certain most learned Theologians leave it undecided.
pass_b_english: Whether the intellect contributes more to man's freedom than the will, or the will more than the intellect, is not something the theologian needs to settle. Aristotle himself, the prince of today's philosophers, did not inquire into it closely.
So we too, along with some very learned theologians, leave the question open.

choices.why: Le Blanc means Aristotle's standing in the schools of his own day; 'today's philosophers' keeps the phrase.
